notes: Fix from the previous version: the button's four legs now have both `joined` and `electrical` edges to the breadboard holes. Before, they only had `joined` edges.

Fix: I corrected which legs are the same side. In the picture the two legs in column 10 (one above and one below the centre gap) are one side, and the two legs in column 12 are the other side. The old version put both of side 1's legs in different columns, which would have shorted pin 2 to GND. Now side 1 (1.l, 1.r) is in column 10 and side 2 (2.l, 2.r) is in column 12.

The breadboard image labels its upper half f-j and its lower half a-e. The catalogue calls rows a-e bank 't' and rows f-j bank 'b'. So the image's upper half is catalogue 'b' and its lower half is 't'.
The button legs are drawn in row g (upper half) and row d (lower half). The wire ends are in row c: pin 2 at column 10, GND at column 12. These are my best reading of the picture.
The black wire is drawn at the Arduino power header's second GND pin, which I named GND.2.
Pin 2 uses the internal pull-up (INPUT_PULLUP), so there is no external resistor. Pin 13's onboard LED is built into the Uno and not modelled as a separate part.
The Uno connects to the computer over USB for serial. The manual lists no USB cable part, so none is included.
